historicalIdentity.model: Hungarian-language supplementary afternoon/weekend school in Vienna
historicalIdentity.reason: The 1987 founding and long-term continuity are corroborated by archival press, Austrian public-service and national press, an ELTE scholarly publication, a University of Vienna academic source, minority-community documentation, the Kőrösi Csoma Sándor Program and recent Austrian Hungarian minority media.

independentHistoricalEvidence.title: Bemutatkozik a Bécsi Magyar Iskola
keyFacts: The scholarly publication states that the school was founded in the 1987–1988 school year by the Központi Szövetség and a small committed team.
At the article date it reported 140 learners and 12 groups; these are historical figures only.

independentHistoricalEvidence.publisher: University of Vienna / Studies in European Language Diversity
independentHistoricalEvidence.title: Studies in European Language Diversity 22.2
keyFacts: The academic source states that pupil numbers had continuously increased since the school's founding in 1987.
It reports 190 registered pupils in 2009/10 and documents the 2012 institutional split; both are historical, scope-limited facts.

independentHistoricalEvidence.title: Die Minderheit, die keine sein will
evidenceFor: historical growth linked to young-family migration
keyFacts: The Wiener Zeitung described the Wiener Ungarische Schule in Vienna's first district as having been founded by the Zentralverband more than twenty years earlier.
It reported strong historical growth associated with immigration of young families; quoted learner numbers apply only to the article's school year.

independentHistoricalEvidence.title: Bécsi Napló XXVII. évfolyam 1. szám – Bécsi Magyar Iskola történeti összefoglaló
keyFacts: The weekend Hungarian education program began in September 1987 with about 30–35 pupils.
By 2002, after opening a preschool group, enrollment had reached about 80; subsequent annual totals were around 90–100 in the period described.

independentHistoricalEvidence.publisher: ARGE Volksgruppen / Wiener Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Volksgruppenfragen
independentHistoricalEvidence.title: Die Volksgruppen in Wien
keyFacts: The German-language Vienna minority-community publication states that the Wiener Ungarische Schule has existed since 1987.

independentHistoricalEvidence.title: 30 éves a Bécsi Magyar Iskola
keyFacts: ORF reported the school's 30th anniversary in 2017.
The report identifies Hegedűs Imre János and his wife as founders and the Központi Szövetség as the maintaining federation.

independentHistoricalEvidence.title: Harminc éves a Bécsi Magyar Iskola – jubileumi ünnepség
keyFacts: The article explicitly states that Hegedűs János and Hegedűs Ilona started the school in 1987.
It documents a 30th anniversary event at the Hungarian Embassy in Vienna.

externalDirectoryEvidence.note: Directory presence is discovery evidence only, not proof of founding date or current program details.
Link-directory evidence supports entity discovery but is lower-weight than dated historical or academic sources.

identityDisambiguation.warning: Do not confuse this Bécsi Magyar Iskola (BMI), founded in 1987 and maintained by the Központi Szövetség, with the separate Bécsi Magyar Iskolaegyesület / Ungarischer Schulverein, whose institutional history is much older and which celebrated its 100th anniversary in 2026.
identityDisambiguation.rule: Any source using '100-year school' language must be entity-resolved before attribution.

historicalClaimPolicy.currentness: Historical sources validate institutional history, not current schedules, prices, staff or locations.
historicalClaimPolicy.addressRule: Historical addresses must not override the current canonical BMI address.
historicalClaimPolicy.measurementRule: Historical enrollment or event counts apply only to the date and scope stated by the source.
